title: The occARU model
text: accommodate structural zeros arising species absences site level, model occupancy species s \1, \dots, S site \1, \dots, latent Bernoulli variable, z_{} = 1 indicates occupancy: \begin{aligned}   z_{} &\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli} \left( \psi_{} \right) \\   \psi_{} &= \operatorname{logit}^{-1} \left( {\alpha_\psi}_{[s]} +     {\boldsymbol{\beta_\psi}}_{[s]} {\boldsymbol{X_1}}_{[]} \right), \end{aligned} \tag{1} \boldsymbol{\alpha_\psi} species-level intercepts, \boldsymbol{\beta_\psi} species-level coefficients \boldsymbol{X_1} represents design matrix. occARU accommodates three types predictors: continuous, categorical, ordinal (ordered categorical). Categorical coefficients modeled zero-sum Gaussian variables, ordinal coefficients parameterised via simplex decomposition category differences (Bürkner Charpentier 2020), coefficient corresponds effect highest category. Species-specific coefficients modeled multivariate normal, facilitating inference correlations predictor responses across species. Spatial effects occupancy included design weakly identified absence repeated measures occupancy site level (Doser et al. 2022). Future versions occARU include multi-season occupancy models, spatial random effects appropriate. Stan accommodate discrete parameters (z_{}) marginalised likelihood; however, posterior inference underlying occupancy states performed forward-backward sampling algorithm setting argument latent = TRUE fit_model().

title: The occARU model
text: species counts surveys j \1, \dots, J produce multi-species time series \boldsymbol{y}_{ij} = (y_{ij1}, \dots, y_{ijS}). Rather reducing counts binary detection/non-detection traditional occupancy models (MacKenzie et al. 2002), occARU models counts directly, capitalising magnitude detections. Conditional z_{} = 1, detections modeled Poisson default: \begin{aligned}   y_{ijs} \mid z_{} = 1 &\sim \mathrm{Poisson} \left( \mu_{ijs} \right) \\   \mu_{ijs} &= \exp \Bigl( {\alpha_\mu}_{[s]} +     {\boldsymbol{\beta_\mu}}_{[s]} {\boldsymbol{X_2}}_{[]} +     \boldsymbol{\gamma}_{[s]} {\boldsymbol{X_3}}_{[ij]} \\     & \quad \quad \quad \  + \iota_{}\left(\boldsymbol{} - {\boldsymbol{P_{X_2}}}_{[]} \right) +     \kappa_{js}\left(\boldsymbol{} - {\boldsymbol{P_{X_3}}}_{[j]} \right) \\     & \quad \quad \quad \ + \log \Delta_{ij}\Bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{2} , \Delta_{ij} proportion survey site actively sampling, taking values 0 1, used offsets detection rates \boldsymbol{\mu}_{ij}. species-specific intercepts \boldsymbol{\alpha_\mu} modeled jointly occupancy intercepts bivariate normal facilitate estimating occupancy/detection correlation across species: \begin{pmatrix} {\alpha_\psi}_{[s]} \\ {\alpha_\mu}_{[s]} \end{pmatrix} \sim \mathrm{MVNormal} \left( \begin{pmatrix} \operatorname{logit} \bar{\psi} \\   \log \bar{\mu} \end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix} \tau_\psi^2 & \rho \tau_\psi \tau_\mu \\   \rho \tau_\psi \tau_\mu & \tau_\mu^2 \end{pmatrix} \right). \tag{3} occupancy (Equation 1), \boldsymbol{\beta_\mu} species-level coefficients \boldsymbol{X_2} represents site-level design matrix. Additionally, \boldsymbol{\gamma} species-level coefficients site--survey design matrix \boldsymbol{X_3}, used predictors vary spatio-temporally. , \boldsymbol{\beta_\mu} \boldsymbol{\gamma} modeled multivariate normal explore interspecific correlations detection rate responses site-level site--survey-level predictors. \boldsymbol{X_2} \boldsymbol{X_3} accommodate continuous, categorical, ordinal predictors. handle repeated measures level sites surveys, site (\boldsymbol{\iota}_i) survey (\boldsymbol{\kappa}_j) random effects included default. modeled matrix normal distributions, row covariances Gaussian process (GP) kernels capturing spatial temporal structure, column covariances interspecific covariance matrices capturing correlations across species. formulation accommodates effects may differ magnitude across species nevertheless correlated: \begin{aligned}   \boldsymbol{\iota}_i &\sim \mathrm{MatrixNormal}     \left( \bar{\iota}_i, \boldsymbol{K_{\iota}}, \Sigma_{\iota} \right) \\   \boldsymbol{\kappa}_j &\sim \mathrm{MatrixNormal}     \left( \bar{\kappa}_j, \boldsymbol{K_{\kappa}}, \Sigma_{\kappa} \right). \end{aligned} , \bar{\boldsymbol{\iota}} \bar{\boldsymbol{\kappa}} mean site survey effects, modeled GPs; \boldsymbol{K_{\iota}} \boldsymbol{K_{\kappa}} \times J \times J GP kernels; \Sigma_\iota \Sigma_\kappa S \times S interspecific covariance matrices, respectively. occARU uses exponentiated quadratic kernels: K_{n, n'} = \tau^2 \exp \left(- \frac{\lVert \boldsymbol{x}_n -   \boldsymbol{x}_{n'} \rVert^2}{2\ell^2} \right), \tag{4} \lVert \boldsymbol{x}_n - \boldsymbol{x}_{n'} \rVert Euclidean distance inputs (site UTMs kms survey index), \tau marginal scale GP, \ell length scale controlling rate decay. occARU facilitates fitting species-specific GP kernels; however, requires S additional Cholesky decompositions site survey effects. default, kernel used mean species-specific GP realisations, realisations differing magnitude species-specific scales, requiring one Cholesky decomposition per GP. occARU option include periodic kernel temporal GP kernel \boldsymbol{K_\kappa} (setting periodic_gp = TRUE fit_model()): K_{n, n'} = \tau^2 \exp \left(- \frac{2 \sin^2 \left( \pi   \lvert x_n - x_{n'} \rvert / p \right)}{\ell^2} \right), \tag{5} p period survey units (e.g., 52 annual cycle weekly surveys) \tau \ell interpretation . GP kernels closed addition, single Cholesky decomposition required. variance partition two GP kernels handled via simplex \boldsymbol{K_\phi} = \left({K_\phi}_{[1]}, {K_\phi}_{[2]}\right), \sum_{g=1}^2 {K_\phi}_{[g]} = 1. Site survey random effects can fully disabled fitted without GPs, collapsing multivariate normals, arguments spatial = c("gp", "mvn", "none") temporal = c("gp", "mvn", "none") fit_model(). Identifiability matrix normal scales ensured fixing marginal scale GP kernels 1. predictors included alongside spatial temporal random effects, fixed random effects can confounded random effects absorb part variance fixed effects trying explain (Hodges Reich 2010). One remedy construct random effects orthogonal column space design matrix. Taking spatial random effects example, instead sampling \boldsymbol{\iota}, occARU samples \boldsymbol{\iota} \left(\boldsymbol{} - \boldsymbol{P_{X_2}} \right), \boldsymbol{P_{X_2}} := \boldsymbol{X_2^\prime} \left(\boldsymbol{X_2} \boldsymbol{X_2^\prime} \right)^{-1} \boldsymbol{X_2} \boldsymbol{} - \boldsymbol{P_{X_2}} orthogonal complement column space site-level design matrix \boldsymbol{X_2}. Two extensions beyond basic Poisson observation model available via overdispersion = c("none", "nb", "olre") argument fit_model(): Negative binomial (overdispersion = "nb"): species-specific overdispersion parameter \phi_s estimated, y_{ijs} \mid z_{} = 1 \sim \mathrm{NegBin}(\mu_{ijs}, \phi_s). text: model uses global-local shrinkage priors variance components occupancy detection submodels (Aguilar Bürkner 2023). accommodates wide range model complexity (.e., various number covariates different random effects) principled unified prior framework. occARU places half-Student-t priors variance linear predictor occupancy log odds (W_\psi) log detection rates (W_\mu). variances simplex-decomposed different model components (e.g., species-level intercepts, hierarchical coefficients, random site survey effects, potentially Poisson OLREs). occARU model automatically determines number variance partitions submodel (V_\psi V_\mu) produces prior scales using V-length simplexes \boldsymbol{\phi_\psi} \boldsymbol{\phi_\mu} , e.g., \boldsymbol{\tau_\mu} := \left(\tau_1, \dots, \tau_{V_\mu} \right) = \sqrt{W_\mu \cdot \boldsymbol{\phi_\mu}}. Variance decomposition can done either Dirichlet zero-sum logistic-normal distributions \boldsymbol{\phi}, set via variance_decomposition = c("dirichlet", "logistic-normal") argument fit_model(). either case, hyperparameters \theta_\psi \theta_\mu control concentration sparsity simplex: Dirichlet models, \theta inverse concentration, logistic-normal models, scale. underlying distributions, larger values \theta correspond sparse simplex (.e., small number components account variance), smaller values corresponding concentrated simplexes (.e., different model components evenly account variance). Veriance decomposition also used species-specific scales site survey effects (potentially OLREs). scales vector \boldsymbol{\phi_\mu} contains one partition species-level deviations mean function , simplex decomposed produce species-specific scales. Parameter named fit objects iota_t, kappa_t, epsilon_t, respectively.

text: random effects (species-level intercepts, fixed effect coefficients, site effects, survey effects, OLRE residuals) fit sum--zero constraints parameter identifiability (Ogle Barber 2020). Without constraints, overall intercepts (\bar{\psi} \bar{\mu}), mean effects (.e., \bar{\boldsymbol{\beta}}, \bar{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}, \boldsymbol{\bar{\iota}}, \boldsymbol{\bar{\kappa}}, \boldsymbol{\bar{\epsilon}}) species-level deviations weakly identified. constraints implemented directly Stan parameterisation using sum_to_zero_vector sum_to_zero_matrix types, induce constraint favourable posterior geometry leading increased computational efficiency. title: The occARU model
text: occARU produces site--species level log likelihoods (log_lik) generated quantities; values can used Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-cross-validation (PSIS-LOO-CV, Vehtari et al. 2017) implemented loo package (Vehtari et al. 2025). PSIS-LOO-CV known problematic observation-level parameters, .e. \iota_{} , OLREs included, \epsilon_{ijs}. remedy, Monte Carlo integration random effects used produce second log likelihood object (log_lik2), user can set number Monte Carlo draws perform per HMC iteration (argument loo_draws fit_model()). Posterior predictions can produced y_{ijs} Q_{} := \sum_{j=1}^J y_{ijs}, setting argument ppc = c("Q", "y", "", "none") fit_model(). facilitates posterior predictive checking, .e. via bayesplot package (Gabry et al. 2025). Additionally, log prior density prior hyperparameters stored (lprior), facilitating prior predictive checking via priorsense package (Kallioinen et al. 2023).

title: Occupancy Models for Automated Recording Unit (ARU) Data
text: occARU fits Bayesian (multispecies) occupancy models count observation models autonomous recording unit (ARU) data like derived camera traps passive acoustic monitoring. approach differs standard occupancy models focus quantifying detection rates, rather treating detection nuisance parameter correct . implements hierarchical species-level random effects spatial temporal Gaussian processes, variance decomposition via global-local shrinkage priors, built Stan via cmdstanr.

title: Occupancy Models for Automated Recording Unit (ARU) Data
text: Install occARU GitHub: occARU requires CmdStan >= 2.36.0. used Stan , run: checks C++ toolchain installs CmdStan automatically.
code: # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("mhollanders/occARU") library(occARU) setup_occARU()

title: Occupancy Models for Automated Recording Unit (ARU) Data
text: make_data() accepts deployment observation data frames following camtrapDP format:
code: data <- make_data(   deployments = deployments,   observations = observations,   failures = failures  # also accepts failure dates per site   survey_length = 14, # aggregate to 2-weekly survey periods   thin_minutes = 30  # thin observations to 30 minutes, retaining highest count   detection_site_predictors = site_predictors,   survey_predictors = survey_predictors  ) data #> ── occARU data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sites (I): 30 #> Surveys (J): 114 #> Species (S): 6 #> Detections: 11463 #> Site coordinates: yes #> Deployment span: 2019-11-06 to 2024-03-06 #> Survey length: 14 days #> Thinning: 30 minutes #> Occupancy site predictors: 0 #> Detection site predictors: 5 #>   Continuous: 3 #>   Categorical: 1 #>   Ordinal: 1 #> Survey predictors: 4 #>   Continuous: 3 #>   Categorical: 0 #>   Ordinal: 1

title: Occupancy Models for Automated Recording Unit (ARU) Data
text: default fits model spatial temporal Gaussian processes, Dirichlet variance decomposition, Poisson observation model, initialised Pathfinder across 4 chains. See ?fit_model ?set_priors customise model structure priors.
code: # set some priors for hyperparameters (unspecified use defaults) priors <- set_priors(   psi_bar = c(1, 2),  # Beta(1, 2) for mean occupancy   mu_W = c(3, 0, 1)   # Student-t+(3, 0, 1) for log detection variance ) #> ── occARU priors ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> psi_bar: Beta(1, 2) #> mu_bar: Gamma(1, 1) #> psi_W: Student-t+(3, 0, 1) #> mu_W: Student-t+(3, 0, 1) #> psi_theta: Gamma(1, 1) #> ...  # fit the model fit <- fit_model(data, prior = priors)

title: Occupancy Models for Automated Recording Unit (ARU) Data
text: model stores marginal site--species log likelihoods (log_lik), log prior density (lprior), posterior predictions full detection history (yrep) aggregated site--species counts (Qrep). Optionally, Monte Carlo integration site observation-level random effects produces marginal log likelihoods (log_lik2) improved PSIS-LOO-CV performance.
code: # use PSIS-LOO-CV on the site-by-species level log likelihood fit$loo("log_lik2")  # log_lik2 uses Monte Carlo integration of random effects  # check prior sensitivity using power-scaling priorsense::powerscale_plot_dens(fit$draws("log_lik", "lprior", "psi_bar"))  # posterior predictive checking of aggregated site-by-species counts bayesplot::pp_check(apply(data$y, c(1, 3), sum) |> c(),                     yrep = fit$draws("Qrep", format = "draws_matrix"),                     group = rep(attr(data, "species"), each = data$I),                     fun = "ppc_rootogram_grouped")

title: Fit the occARU model — fit_model
text: data occARU_data object produced make_data(). stan_file character. Path custom Stan file. NULL (default), uses built-multispecies occARU model, single species version one species included. Intended advanced users modified Stan program; note custom models likely require corresponding changes output make_data(). spatial character. Structure site-level random effects. "gp" (default) fits hierarchical multi-species spatial Gaussian process exponentiated quadratic kernel, recommended option. "mvn" fits unstructured multivariate normal, "none" omits site-level random effects entirely. temporal character. Structure survey-level random effects. "gp" (default) fits hierarchical multi-species temporal Gaussian process exponentiated quadratic kernel, recommended option. "mvn" fits unstructured multivariate normal, "none" omits survey-level random effects entirely. periodic_gp logical. TRUE, periodic kernel added temporal GP kernel. used temporal = "gp". Default: FALSE. period Positive numeric. Period length survey units (.e. number survey periods per cycle). used temporal = "gp" periodic_gp = TRUE. Defaults 365 / survey_length, corresponding annual cycle. example, survey_length = 7 default period = 52.1. Override data span different temporal cycle. species_length_scales logical. TRUE, species-specific GP length scales estimated kernel, drawn independently shared length scale priors. Note enabling requires additional Cholesky decompositions per species GP per iteration, can substantially increase sampling time. FALSE (default), one Cholesky decomposition performed per GP. used multiple species included, spatial = "gp" temporal = "gp". project_kappa logical. TRUE (default), uses orthogonal projection random survey effects using site-averaged survey predictor design matrix. Ignored survey predictors provided. overdispersion character. Overdispersion model observation process. One "none" (Poisson, default), "nb" (negative binomial), "olre" (correlated observation-level random effects). variance_decomposition character. Prior variance partitions. One "dirichlet" (default) "logistic-normal". latent logical. TRUE (default), latent occupancy states z recovered species using forward-backward sampling algorithm. loo_draws Non-negative integer. Number Monte Carlo draws marginal log-likelihood estimation site-level random effects /Poisson OLREs PSI-LOO-CV via loo::loo(). Default: 100, produces additional [S, ] matrix log_lik2 marginalising site effects (OLRE residuals applicable) via Monte Carlo integration. log_lik2 recommended log_lik PSIS-LOO-CV produces better Pareto-k diagnostics. Set 0 disable, returning log_lik. used spatial "none" overdispersion = "olre". ppc character. Posterior predictive checks compute. One "Q" (default), "y", "", "none". "y" returns full [, J, S] prediction array (yrep); "Q" returns aggregated counts [, S] (Qrep). large datasets, "Q" "none" can substantially reduce memory usage sampling time. prior occARU_priors object set_priors(). omitted, default priors used. init character, numeric, list. Initialisation strategy passed cmdstanr::CmdStanModel$sample(). One : "pathfinder" Default. Use pathfinder generate initial values (see cmdstanr::CmdStanModel$pathfinder()). Recommended complex models can substantially reduce warmup time improve convergence. numeric scalar Initialise parameters uniformly \([-\)init\(,\) init\(]\). list Custom initial values passed directly cmdstanr::CmdStanModel$sample(). pathfinder_args Named list additional arguments passed cmdstanr::CmdStanModel$pathfinder() init = "pathfinder". Overrides defaults (refresh = 0, sig_figs = 14, init = 0.1, num_paths = chains, num_threads = chains). Default: list(). threads Positive integer. Number threads within-chain parallelisation via reduce_sum(). Default: 1 (parallelisation). total number threads used threads * chains, optimal performance set threads = floor(available_cores / chains). example, 8 cores 4 chains gives threads = 2. grainsize Positive integer. Chunk size (number sites) within-chain parallelisation via reduce_sum(). used threads > 1. Default: 1, lets Stan automatically determine optimal chunk size. Increase many sites want reduce parallelisation overhead. See Stan User's Guide details tuning grainsize. ... Additional arguments passed cmdstanr::CmdStanModel$pathfinder(). Uses parallel chains default. sampling arguments use Stan defaults.

Default: deploymentEnd. latitude <data-masking> numeric. Column name WGS84 latitude deployments. omitted alongside longitude, spatial Gaussian process fitted. Default: latitude. longitude <data-masking> numeric. Column name WGS84 longitude deployments. Default: longitude. eventStart <data-masking> POSIXt. Column name observation timestamps observations. Observations aggregated within survey period summing count, recording effort (Delta) computed fraction survey length ARU active. example, survey_length = 7 aggregates weekly survey periods, Delta ranging 0 (ARU failed week) 1 (ARU active week). Longer periods reduce number surveys J increase counts per survey, trading temporal resolution model complexity closure assumption within survey period. Default: 1L. thin_minutes Non-negative numeric. supplied, observations within thin_minutes minutes (per site species) thinned single observation, retaining record highest count.
